title: Window and Door Rebates in Langley 2026: $100 Each, Up to $2,000
desc: Langley homes can claim $100 per window or door from BC Hydro. The Township is 82% owner-occupied and the City is 61% apartments. Rules and steps.
h1: Window and Door Rebates in Langley
lead: Langley's two municipalities have different housing. In the Township most households own a house, and the window rebate fits them well. In the City, most households live in apartments, which the program does not cover.
cards_heading: What BC Hydro pays for windows and doors in Langley
cards_intro: We re-read BC Hydro's window and door page on October 2, 2026. The rebate is for homes heated mainly by electricity. FortisBC lists $100 per opening for its gas customers, except in the City of Vancouver.

cards.title: Windows and doors
cards.note: Paid for each window or door that replaces an existing one between a heated space and outdoors.

cards.title: Cap
cards.note: That is 20 openings at $100 each. A bay window counts as one opening.

cards.title: Energy rating
cards.note: The window or door must have a maximum U-factor of 1.22 W/m2-K, which is BC Hydro's Tier 2 level.

cards.title: More than one upgrade
cards.note: BC Hydro adds a bonus when you finish more than one eligible upgrade.

cards.title: Lower incomes
cards.note: Income-qualified customers can apply for free upgrades.

after_cards:
A Township two-storey

A house with 13 windows, a front door and a patio door is 15 openings. That pays 15 x $100 = $1,500. An outbuilding such as a workshop or barn earns nothing, even if you replace its windows at the same time.
sections: The 2021 Census counted 46,925 households in the Township of Langley and 12,600 in the City of Langley. In the Township, 23% live in pre-1981 homes, 82% own and only 10% live in apartments. In the City, 38% live in older homes but 61% are in apartments. Across both, about 15,705 households (26%) live in homes built before 1981, and 8,405 of those are owner-occupied detached houses.

Much of the Township is farm and acreage land. The program covers the home, not garages, shops, barns or other outbuildings. The home must be a year-round primary residence, at least 12 months old. A cabin or vacation home does not qualify.
Langley's average January low from 2015 to 2024 was 0.3°C and the coldest day was -16.8°C. Winters are mild and wet. The gains from new windows are mainly less condensation and fewer drafts.

Each rough opening where a window or door was replaced counts as one. A bay window is one opening. Skylights are excluded. Each unit must have a U-factor of 1.22 W/m2-K or lower and carry a listing from CSA, Intertek, Labtest, QAI or NFRC.

The rebate needs a U-factor of 1.22 W/m2-K or lower, and lower means less heat loss. Many window labels show the older imperial scale instead. To convert, multiply the imperial number by 5.678. A label that says U-0.30 equals 1.70 W/m2-K, which is too high. A label that says U-0.21 equals about 1.19 W/m2-K and passes. Ask the contractor to quote the metric value for each model so you do not have to convert.

Windows and attic insulation both cut heat loss. If your budget only covers one, compare each rebate to its quote rather than the headline cap: walls and basements pay $0.09 per R per square foot, while windows pay a flat $100 per opening. If you can do both, apply together and ask about the bonus.

BC Hydro sends income-qualified customers to the CleanBC Better Homes Energy Savings Program instead, and the two cannot be combined. The 2026 program document lists no insulation or window rebates, so the free Energy Conservation Assistance Program is the route to ask about.
claim_steps: Check your home is a house or row home with its own meter, not a condo.
Get quotes that list the U-factor of each unit.
Photograph each label on installation day.
Keep the invoice and apply within six months.
Add insulation to the same application to check the bonus.
faq: Does a barn or workshop count?
Can I claim in the City of Langley if I live in a condo?
No. Condos and apartments are not eligible for this program.
How many openings can I claim?
Yes. BC Hydro asks for the invoice and photos of each manufacturer label.
What if I heat with gas?
FortisBC lists $100 per opening for gas customers.
